newsitem.title: CHINA: China's B share indices end down on concerns.
newsitem.headline: China's B share indices end down on concerns.

text.p: China's B share indices ended lower on Wednesday on concerns about poor 1996 company results and the possibility of new concrete measures to keep domestic investors from buying B shares, brokers said.
Shanghai's B index fell 1.59 percent to 69.752 points on turnover of $7.6 million, against Tuesday's $10.4 million.
Shenzhen's B index lost 1.17 percent to close at 167.66 points. Turnover was HK$109.7 million ($14.2 million) compared with Tuesday's HK$216.7 million.
"Investors are reluctant to buy stakes with high risks during the company reporting season," a Shenzhen analyst at China Guotai Securities said.

Shanghai brokers said that market talk that Beijing would take measures this week to force domestic investors out of B share trading dampened market sentiment, compounded by poor performance in the A share market.
China's securities authorities have several times reaffirmed the ban on domestic investors buying B shares but they have yet to translate it into effective measures, brokers said.
In Shanghai, Shanghai Lianhua Fibre was the biggest loser on expectations of poor 1996 results, plunging $0.020 or 9.09 percent to $0.200 on volume of 30,000 shares.
Real estate developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development was the most active, falling $0.010 or 1.04 percent to $0.950 on volume of 1.5 million shares on profit-taking.
In Shenzhen, beverage maker Shenzhen Shenbao Industrial Co Ltd was the biggest loser, dropping HK$0.24 or 3.84 percent to HK$6.01.
Meanwhile, the A share indices ended mixed on consolidation, with Shanghai's A share index down 0.08 percent to 1,216.271 points and Shenzhen's A index up 0.71 percent to 428.77 points.
In Shanghai, Tianjin Global Magnetic Card A share was the biggest loser on profit-taking, slipping 7.35 percent to 28.90 yuan ($3.48) on volume of 1.2 million shares.
In Shenzhen, the best performing A share was television tube maker Shenzhen SEG Co Ltd, which rose to its 10 percent limit-up of 17.79 yuan on volume of 55.2 million shares.
